abstract: Coupling of immunohistochemistry with MALDI mass spectroscopy (MALDI-IHC) enables targeted spatial analysis of proteins through the use of photocleavable mass tags. Upwards of 100 proteins can be imaged in a single run due to the high multiplexing power of this technology. Coupled with mass shifts in MALDI-IHC data, this scalability creates a challenge for users, as there are currently no dedicated software tools for MALDI-IHC data processing. Here we introduce gutenTAG, an open-source processing and quality control tool specifically designed for MALDI-IHC. gutenTAG uses a novel strategy based on grouping clusters of m/z bins originating from the same molecular species into single entities termed metapeaks. This strategy is robust to mass shift, generating ion images that capture the full signal of peaks corresponding to each mass tag while minimizing noise. Furthermore, we show that the metapeak strategy can be adapted to alternative open-source tools to facilitate their use in targeted imaging applications.
